top.title: Ogun: INEC silent as court orders it to restore Adebutu’s name within 24hrs
top.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Independent National Electoral Commission INEC has yet to react officially to a Federal High Court judgment directing it to publish Oladipupo Adebutu’s name as the Peoples Democratic Party PDP candidate for the 2027 Ogun governorship election, saying it only read about the ruling on social media. The Director of Voter Education and Publicity at INEC, Mrs Victoria Messi-Eta, said she read about the judgment in the media and would get a response from the commission’s legal department. As of the time of filing this report, she had yet to revert. The National Commissioner in charge of Voter Education and Publicity, Malam Mohammed Haruna, neither returned calls nor responded to messages sent to him on the matter. The commission’s silence came after Justice Peter Lifu of the Federal High Court in Abuja ordered INEC on Friday to publish Adebutu’s name within 24 hours. Delivering judgment, Justice Lifu held that INEC had no powers to unilaterally remove the name of a validly nominated candidate by a political party. He held that the commission’s action was unconstitutional, unlawful and of no effect. The judge said only the Federal High Court or the state high court had the power to declare a candidate invalid, not the commission. He also held that INEC breached Adebutu’s right to fair hearing, and dismissed the commission’s preliminary objection, declaring the suit competent. The PDP and Adebutu filed the suit on Oct. 22 after his name was removed from the list of contestants for the Ogun governorship seat. INEC was the sole defendant. Their lawyer, Ahmed Raji, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN), sought 11 reliefs, including an order setting aside the commission’s decision to omit, remove or refuse to publish Adebutu’s name in the final list of candidates published on Oct. 10, for denial of fair hearing and violation of Sections 29 and 32 of the Electoral Act, 2026. They also asked the court to compel “the defendant to, within twenty-four (24) hours of the order/orders of this honourable court, include and/or publish the name of the 2nd plaintiff as the 1st plaintiff’s governorship candidate for Ogun State in the forthcoming 2027 General Election.” The post Ogun: INEC silent as court orders it to restore Adebutu’s name within 24hrs appeared first on Vanguard News .

top.title: Red Sox's Jake Bauers Deal Pretty Much Spells End For Jarren Duran, Masataka Yoshida
top.description: Boston Red Sox outfielder Jarren Duran The Boston Red Sox have reportedly agreed to a four-year, $58 million deal with Jake Bauers. According to MassLive's Chris Cotillo , the Red Sox plan to use Bauers "primarily as their designated hitter while also cycling him in at first base in an effort to get Willson Contreras off his feet." If that's the case, Jarren Duran and Masataka Yoshida may need to pack their bags. Bauers plays first base and can fill in as a left fielder or right fielder. He'll be in the lineup every day, and if he's primarily taking the designated hitter spot, Duran and Yoshida will be bench bats or, at best, extra outfielders. The problem is, both will be very expensive bench players. Duran could end up getting $11.1 million in arbitration, per MLB Trade Rumors' estimate , and Yoshida is due $18.6 million next season. Those are some large figures for players who won't play regularly. The Red Sox have Roman Anthony, Ceddanne Rafaela and Wilyer Abreu in the outfield. Bauers can fill in if needed, and if the Red Sox don't want him there, they may much rather give Kristian Campbell a spot as the team's fourth outfielder. Campbell is already signed to an extension and started playing well in Triple-A toward the end of the season. Regardless, Duran and Yoshida simply don't have a path to regular at-bats with Bauers now on the team. Not only that, but neither one is really irreplaceable. The Red Sox could move on from both and find a much more cost-effective bench bat or two on the open market. More MLB: Cubs Superstar Wins 2026 NL MVP After Historic Season

top.title: Tennessee on upset alert at Texas A&M, college football model warns
top.description: On paper, you wouldn’t think that Tennessee was in any real danger against Texas A&M. Not when considering the general direction these teams have taken this season. But one of the most cited college football prediction models is taking a different view. Model projects a very close game Oct 17, 2026; Knoxville, Tennessee, USA; Tennessee Volunteers defensive back Dejuan Lane (10) celebrates after recovering a fumble against the Alabama Crimson Tide during the first half at Neyland Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Randy Sartin-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Looking over the matchup, ESPN’s College Football Power Index model still likes the Volunteers over the Aggies. But by a very narrow margin. After simulating the game 20,000 times, the model favors Tennessee to be just three points better than Texas A&M on the same field. That’s a much closer gap than most Vols fans would expect against an Aggie squad that has one win in SEC play. Normally, Tennessee is 13 points better than its opponents on average, ranking 17th in FBS in margin of victory. More: Predicting SEC football scores in Week 11’s biggest games Why such a close game? Tennessee has been extremely effective getting after opposing quarterbacks, but there’s one potential downside: the Volunteers have struggled at times to contain quarterbacks who can escape the pocket and extend plays. That’s where Marcel Reed becomes particularly dangerous. Tennessee’s defensive staff has acknowledged the challenge of defending mobile quarterbacks, emphasizing the importance of maintaining disciplined pass-rush lanes against Reed when he takes off. If Tennessee’s defensive ends get too aggressive pursuing the quarterback, Reed can step up, escape outside, and turn broken plays into significant gains. That creates two problems for the Volunteers: Scrambling yards: Reed can punish Tennessee when its pass rush loses lane discipline. Extended passing plays: When Reed escapes pressure, Tennessee’s secondary must cover receivers longer, increasing the possibility of explosive plays. More: SEC power rankings entering college football Week 11 The bottom line Texas A&M doesn’t necessarily need to beat Tennessee with traditional drop-back passing plays. The Aggies can use Reed’s mobility to neutralize some of Tennessee’s pass-rush advantage and force the Volunteers to defend the entire field. The potential breaking point: Tennessee’s inability to keep Marcel Reed contained inside the pocket. top.title: Real Madrid, Manchester United monitoring Serie A midfielder who could cost €25-30 million – report
top.description: Real Madrid, Manchester United monitoring Serie A midfielder who could cost €25-30 million – report According to reports from Calciomercato (h/t Bernabeu Digital ), Real Madrid are closely monitoring the situation of Scott McTominay at Napoli. The Scotland international could become available in the summer amid uncertainty over his contract situation, with Los Blancos among several clubs keeping an eye on developments. McTominay-Mourinho reunion? A product of the Manchester United academy, McTominay became a regular at Old Trafford precisely during Jose Mourinho’s managerial stint at the club. The 29-year-old midfielder developed a special bond with the now-Real Madrid manager, which might come into factor if the Merengues do decide to make a move for him in the summer. Real Madrid have been on the lookout for a new midfielder since last summer and links to McTominay have been doing the rounds for a while now. On Real Madrid’s radar. (Photo by Diogo Cardoso/Getty Images) The Scotsman’s current contract with Napoli expires in the summer of 2028 and an agreement over an extension is proving to be difficult to reach. McTominay is seeking an annual salary of up to €8 million, a demand that has complicated discussions with Napoli. As such, there is a possibility that the Serie A outfit decide to part ways with him next summer rather than risk losing him for nothing in 2028. The report even states that the Partenopei prepared to consider offers of between €25 million and €30 million for the Scotland international. No shortage of competition for McTominay However, Real Madrid are not alone in monitoring the midfielder’s situation. Manchester United have also expressed interest in the re-signing their 29-year-old star. A move back to Old Trafford could appeal to the Scottish international considering his past association with the club. Manchester United also interested in McTominay. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images) Meanwhile, AC Milan have also shown significant interest in him, while Aston Villa have also made enquiries about his situation. For Real Madrid, signing a proven midfielder like McTominay, whom Mourinho knows and trusts, could appeal strongly, especially given his contract situation. However, how he would fit into their scheme would be a major question, considering that Mourinho already has Jude Bellingham, Arda Guler, and Federico Valverde, who operate in similar roles. The Merengues could prefer a midfielder of a different profile, someone who is capable of controlling the game and dictating the tempo of their play from the centre.

top.title: Jeremy Fowler reveals three trades the New York Giants tried to make before the deadline
top.description: Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images The NFC East leaders looked at several options for bringing in a new defensive tackle. A narrow loss to the Washington Commanders hasn’t changed the fact that the New York Giants are in a strong position. However, John Harbaugh’s side could have looked to strengthen before the deadline, with ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler recently explaining what they were looking at and why it didn’t come to fruition. Vita Vea and Jeffery Simmons were among New York Giants targets says Jeremy Fowler When appearing on The Rich Eisen Show , Jeremy Fowler revealed that the New York Giants were looking at two positions before the deadline. They didn’t get a running back option through the door, though Cam Skattebo’s recent performances show that this position may not need strengthening at this time. Fowler did say that the other position in consideration for an “upgrade”, defensive tackle, was the bigger priority for the Giants. He added that Tampa’s Vita Vea and recent Chicago Bears addition Jeffery Simmons were both looked at as options. “At the end of the day, I don’t think they were really willing to give up what it would have taken to get any of those types of star players,” Fowler explained. He went on to name Indianapolis’ Grover Stewart as another name in the mix, with him being seen as more of a “middle-class” option. “They probably could have got him for a fourth-round pick and a little bit more,” Fowler said. “They didn’t have a fourth-round pick coming up. They’re missing a four and a five, so that was part of the equation. “This is a team that was going to try to upgrade, but I wasn’t wholly convinced they were going to go all the way with it because they’re still a little bit in transition roster-wise,” he continued. The Giants will host the Jacksonville Jaguars, who lead the AFC South following back-to-back wins, on November 22. top.description: BYU wide receiver Parker Kingston (11) looks back as he scores a touchdown during the second half of the game against the UCF Knights at LaVell Edwards Stadium in Provo on Saturday, Nov. 29, 2025. | Rio Giancarlo, Deseret News Shortly after the Washington County attorney refiled a rape charge against Parker Kingston on Thursday, the former BYU football star’s lawyers asked a judge to remove the prosecutor and his office from the case. Defense attorneys Cara Tangaro and Scott Williams argue in a 35-page motion in 5th District Court in St. George, Utah, that Jerry Jaeger’s interest in prosecuting the case extends beyond obtaining justice. “A prosecutor’s interest in a criminal case ‘is not that it shall win a case, but that justice shall be done,’” the lawyers wrote, citing a 1935 U.S Supreme Court ruling. ”The Washington County Attorney no longer has only that interest in this case. He has acquired others." On Thursday, Jaeger charged Kingston, 22, with one count of first-degree felony rape for allegedly sexually assaulting a 20-year-old woman in her St. George apartment on Feb. 23, 2025. Kingston was originally arrested and charged with the same crime in February 2026. He was initially held in jail before being released on bail. Fifth District Judge Jay Winward denied prosecutors’ request to delay the trial after they told him the alleged victim was not ready to testify and dismissed the case last June. What Kingston’s and the woman’s lawyers say “With the support of the alleged victim, I have made the decision to refile the case and proceed with this prosecution based on the totality of the evidence,” Jaeger said in a statement. Andrew Deesing, a lawyer for the woman identified in court documents as A.M., said he’s grateful for Jaeger’s and his office’s determination to pursue the case. “Their decision to refile these charges has renewed my client’s faith in the justice system and her belief that her voice will be heard,” he said in a statement. “She has shown extraordinary courage and resolve throughout this process. We look forward to seeing this matter proceed through the courts and to the pursuit of justice.” Tangaro and William said in a statement that Kingston has always maintained and continues to maintain his innocence. top.title: Joe Burrow Could Make NFL History vs. Steelers
top.description: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow during a game against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sept. 27, 2026. -- Ed Thompson Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow could tie a significant NFL record on Sunday night against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Burrow has had four total touchdowns during Cincinanti’s four-game winning streak. He’s tied with Drew Brees (2018) and Dan Marino (1984) for second all time. Burrow will tie Peyton Manning (5) for the most consecutive 4+ total touchdown games in a single season if he accomplishes the feat on Sunday night against the Steelers. Manning set the record in 2004. While the Steelers had a bye in Week 9, the Bengals beat the Atlanta Falcons, 34-17, on Sunday in Madrid. Cincinnati’s offense has been red-hot lately. top.title: Giants’ Jameis Winston Sings ‘Who Let the Dogs Out’ in Failed Attempt to Trick Opponents Into Penalty
top.description: Jameis Winston Credit: Kathryn Riley/Getty NEED TO KNOW Jameis Winston tried to have some fun at the Commanders’ expense on Thursday night The Giants quarterback sang the chorus from the Baha Men’s “Who Let the Dogs Out” to try to draw the team offsides Despite his effort, Washington didn’t fall for the trick Jameis Winston unlocked a new level of quarterback behavior while trying to draw the Washington Commanders offsides on Thursday night. Inserted late into the game for starter J.J. McCarthy on a short 4th-and-1 opportunity, the New York Giants backup barked the chorus of the Baha Men’s “Who Let the Dogs Out” in an attempt to catch the Commanders by surprise. “Who let the dogs out?” Winston, 32, screamed at the line of scrimmage. “Who! Who!” The hilarious moment was not lost on the Thursday Night Football crew in the booth. “You got to be kidding me!” Al Michaels said as the microphones picked up what Winston was laying down. Jameis Winston Credit: Sarah Stier/Getty “What is he doing?” analyst Kirk Herbstreit joked. Alas, Winston’s rendition of the Baha Men’s 2000 classic did little to fool the Commanders’ defense. The Giants took a five-yard penalty and punted from their 11-yard-line — later losing the game 24-21 to the division rival. Winston’s antics hardly surprised his teammates or coach John Harbaugh. “Yeah, I knew that,” Harbaugh later said about Winston’s canine-influenced cadence. “That was part of the cadence there. That was part of the cadence. Teams do jump in those situations sometimes. That was the idea.” Following the game, the Broadway aficionado explained his unusual snap call. “Just practicing that with the team,” Winston told reporters. “The defenses are trying to jump the rhythm. Came up with that. Wish we could’ve got them to jump offsides.” For fans of the unconventional backup, the lyrical moment also came as little surprise. nigeria.title: Ogun: INEC silent as court orders it to restore Adebutu’s name within 24hrs
nigeria.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Independent National Electoral Commission INEC has yet to react officially to a Federal High Court judgment directing it to publish Oladipupo Adebutu’s name as the Peoples Democratic Party PDP candidate for the 2027 Ogun governorship election, saying it only read about the ruling on social media. The Director of Voter Education and Publicity at INEC, Mrs Victoria Messi-Eta, said she read about the judgment in the media and would get a response from the commission’s legal department. As of the time of filing this report, she had yet to revert. The National Commissioner in charge of Voter Education and Publicity, Malam Mohammed Haruna, neither returned calls nor responded to messages sent to him on the matter. The commission’s silence came after Justice Peter Lifu of the Federal High Court in Abuja ordered INEC on Friday to publish Adebutu’s name within 24 hours. Delivering judgment, Justice Lifu held that INEC had no powers to unilaterally remove the name of a validly nominated candidate by a political party. He held that the commission’s action was unconstitutional, unlawful and of no effect. The judge said only the Federal High Court or the state high court had the power to declare a candidate invalid, not the commission. He also held that INEC breached Adebutu’s right to fair hearing, and dismissed the commission’s preliminary objection, declaring the suit competent. The PDP and Adebutu filed the suit on Oct. 22 after his name was removed from the list of contestants for the Ogun governorship seat. INEC was the sole defendant. Their lawyer, Ahmed Raji, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN), sought 11 reliefs, including an order setting aside the commission’s decision to omit, remove or refuse to publish Adebutu’s name in the final list of candidates published on Oct. 10, for denial of fair hearing and violation of Sections 29 and 32 of the Electoral Act, 2026. They also asked the court to compel “the defendant to, within twenty-four (24) hours of the order/orders of this honourable court, include and/or publish the name of the 2nd plaintiff as the 1st plaintiff’s governorship candidate for Ogun State in the forthcoming 2027 General Election.” The post Ogun: INEC silent as court orders it to restore Adebutu’s name within 24hrs appeared first on Vanguard News .

nigeria.title: Prophet, another arraigned over Toluwanisings’ corpse filming, false claims
nigeria.description: By Ayobami Okerinde The Oyo State Police Command has arraigned two men over the unauthorised filming and online circulation of the remains of late gospel singer Olayemi Bayonle Bolaji, popularly known as Toluwanisings, as well as social media allegations linking his family members to his death. The command announced this in a statement issued on Friday by its Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Ayanlade Olayinka. One of the defendants, Prophet Moses Idowu, was arrested after visiting the morgue where the singer’s body was deposited, claiming he had the spiritual ability to bring the dead back to life. The police said, “In the course of the incident, the suspect recorded a video of the deceased’s body and subsequently circulated the footage on social media without the consent or authorisation of the deceased’s family, thereby subjecting the remains to indignity and causing further distress to the bereaved family.” It further accused Idowu of publishing claims that the singer’s wife, Olayemi Elizabeth Damilola, and his manager were responsible for his death, without providing evidence to support the allegations. He was subsequently charged with four offences, including unlawful recording and publication, defamation, treating a deceased person’s body in an undignified manner and conduct capable of disturbing public peace. The court ordered that Idowu be held at a correctional facility and adjourned the case until December 2, 2026. In a separate case, the police arraigned another man, Oladapo Joshua Dunminimnun, following his arrest on Thursday, November 12, over alleged defamatory and unsubstantiated social media posts concerning the singer’s death. The command said Dunminimnun shared videos accusing the deceased’s personal assistant and members of his family of having a hand in his death. It added that investigations showed he continued making the publications despite knowing about an undertaking signed by the parties involved, which prohibited individuals from publishing material about the deceased through print or other media. The police also said the posts persisted despite repeated warnings from the family and the command against spreading unverified claims. Dunminimnun was charged with offences relating to the publication of false information on Facebook, unlawful publication of defamatory material and conduct likely to cause a breach of public peace. His case was adjourned until December 11, 2026, for further proceedings. The police expressed concern over the circulation of unverified allegations and sensitive images on social media, particularly when they involve deceased persons and grieving relatives. nigeria.title: Old anthem sung spontaneously, new one followed at NDC event — Doherty
nigeria.description: By Ayobami Okerinde The Lagos State governorship candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Funso Doherty, has said the singing of Nigeria’s former national anthem at the party’s town hall meeting in Lagos was a spontaneous reaction by attendees. Doherty, who spoke on Nigeria Info 99.3FM on Friday, said the current national anthem was also sung after the crowd had recited the former version. He explained that the event organisers could not control the spontaneous reaction of a large gathering, particularly given the emotional atmosphere surrounding the meeting. “Well, the point to be made is that if you watched that show, you will see that the new national anthem was actually sung after that initial singing of the old national anthem, and what happened was it was a spontaneous thing by the crowd,” he said. He added that the official anthem was eventually performed, insisting that Nigeria had only one national anthem. “Obviously, the national anthem is the national anthem. We only have one national anthem, and ultimately that was what we sang,” he said. Doherty’s explanation followed Thursday’s incident at the NDC town hall meeting in Lagos , where the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, and other attendees declined to stand when invited to sing the current national anthem. The event anchor subsequently switched to the former anthem, “Arise, O Compatriots”, which Obi, Doherty and other supporters sang. The incident has attracted criticism from Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, and Nigeria’s Ambassador to Mexico, Reno Omokri. Wike, who spoke at a stakeholders’ town hall in Ogu-Bolo Local Government Area of Rivers State on Friday, accused Obi of disrespecting Nigeria’s national symbols. He said Obi’s decision not to stand for the current anthem, but to join in singing the former version, raised questions about his commitment to the country. “A whole national anthem of a country is being sung. A man who wants to be President of Nigeria would disobey and sit down. And then not only that, when a different national anthem that is not being used for Nigeria was sung, he stood up,” Wike said. He added that anyone who disrespected the national anthem should not aspire to lead the country. “A man who does not believe in Nigeria, someone who derives joy in ridiculing the country by disrespecting its symbolic National Anthem must not be allowed to come near the presidency of our country,” he said. Similarly, Omokri criticised Obi and NDC supporters, describing the Constitution, national anthem and national football team as apolitical symbols that unite Nigerians. nigeria.title: Flamingos players shift focus to career development after World Cup success
nigeria.description: Players of Nigeria’s Under-17 women’s national team, the Flamingos, say they have shifted focus to personal and career development following their triumph at the 2026 FIFA Under-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. The players told the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) in separate interviews that although winning the competition was a major achievement, it marked only the beginning of their football careers. The captain of the team, Chidi Harmony, said the players must put the achievement behind them and concentrate on correcting their mistakes and improving their individual performances. “This is just a starting point. We cannot look at this success and say we have arrived. As young players, we have to put this aside and focus on development. “It is time to work on our mistakes. We want to go out every day and keep improving ourselves so that we can win more trophies for the country,” Harmony said. On her personal ambitions, Harmony said she had identified four or five top European clubs she hoped to play for but declined to disclose their names. “I have four or five big clubs I want to play for, but I will keep them to myself for now. I will share the names the day I finally sign for any of the clubs,” she said. Similarly, Golden Ball winner, Oluebube Umejiaku, expressed gratitude to God for the team’s success in Morocco, saying she was already looking forward to greater achievements. She recalled that following their triumph at the WAFU B tournament in Cote d’Ivoire, the team had resolved to replicate the feat at the World Cup. “After the WAFU B in Cote d’Ivoire, where we won, we told ourselves that we would go and do the same in Morocco, and I am very happy we returned home with the trophy. “Personally, I feel I have not even started. This is just the beginning of my career, and I pray that God helps me achieve more and win more trophies for the country,” Umejiaku said. Forward Kemi Adegbuyi also said she remained determined to achieve greater success, adding that she was focused on improving her game and making further impact in football. She expressed gratitude to God, her family and supporters for their contributions to her success. “I am very happy and grateful to God, my family and those who have been supporting me. “But now, I am focusing on not letting my guard down. I am concentrating on improving myself and making more statements in football,” Adegbuyi said. The FC Robo forward also called for increased investment and support for the Nigerian women’s league to enable more talented players to showcase their abilities. According to her, the league has many undiscovered talents who require adequate platforms and opportunities to develop their careers. “There are a lot of hidden talents in the women’s league in Nigeria. We just need the right platforms to showcase our talents. “We need more investment and support,” she said. nigeria.title: Tinubu flags off $3.5bn Bakassi Deep Seaport construction
nigeria.description: President Bola Tinubu on Friday flagged off the construction of the 3.5 billion dollar Bakassi Deep Seaport in Cross River. Tinubu, represented by the vice-president, Kashim Shettima, described the project as a historic economic intervention capable of transforming Nigeria’s maritime industry. Speaking at the groundbreaking ceremony in Bakassi, Tinubu said the project would break a centuries-old jinx and reposition Cross River as a major commercial and maritime hub. “I have not come to Calabar to cut a ribbon and dance Ekpe Masquerade. I am here to break ground and break centuries-old jinx,” he said. He said the project would unlock Nigeria’s maritime potential, diversify the economy and demonstrate what collective commitment could achieve. The President said the seaport, supported by a proposed superhighway, would provide an evacuation corridor linking the South-South to other parts of the country. He said the concentration of more than 80 per cent of Nigeria’s foreign trade through Lagos ports had contributed to congestion, shipment delays and higher costs. “Lagos is not our enemy. Lagos is our elder brother in faith. No country eats with one hand. No country carries all its load on one shoulder. “When over 80 per cent of our foreign trade flows through Lagos, and Lagos alone, that is not strength. That is congestion,” he said. Tinubu said the Bakassi project would complement existing ports, improve cargo movement and strengthen Nigeria’s competitiveness in international trade. nigeria.title: AFCONQ: Arokodare scores brace as Super Eagles defeat Tanzania 3-1
nigeria.description: The Super Eagles of Nigeria bounced back to winning ways in their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations, AFCON qualifying campaign with a 3-1 victory over Tanzania at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium in Uyo on Friday. Nigeria took an early lead through Alhassan Yusuf, who found the back of the net in the third minute to give the hosts a promising start. However, Tanzania fought back and restored parity in the 36th minute after Wilfred Ndidi lost possession in midfield, allowing Msanga to capitalise on slack defending and make it 1-1. The Super Eagles suffered another setback before the break when Ademola Lookman was forced off with an injury and replaced by Moses Simon. Both teams went into half-time level, with Nigeria seeking to regain their advantage after the restart. Super Eagles coach Eric Chelle introduced Tolu Arokodare and Chidera Usor at the beginning of the second half, replacing Alhassan Yusuf and Raphael Onyedika. The changes paid off as Arokodare restored Nigeria’s lead in the 52nd minute with an excellent flicked finish to make it 2-1. The striker completed his brace in the 60th minute, finishing off a move created by fellow substitute Nsor to extend Nigeria’s advantage to 3-1. Chelle’s men maintained their two-goal cushion in the closing stages, although Arokodare missed an opportunity to complete his hat-trick. The final whistle confirmed a 3-1 victory for Nigeria, giving the Super Eagles a boost in their quest for qualification for the 2027 AFCON. nigeria.title: Man United captain Bruno Fernandes rejects second contract offer
nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has rejected the club’s second offer to extend his contract, leaving negotiations over the Portugal midfielder’s future unresolved. BBC Sport reports that Fernandes is out of contract at the end of the season, although United can extend his deal by 12 months, until 2028. The club wants to agree a new contract before using that option. If no agreement is reached, United are expected to trigger the extension before January 1. Without it, Fernandes would be able to sign a pre-contract agreement with foreign clubs from that date, with six months remaining on his deal. It is unclear when Fernandes rejected the offer. A resolution does not appear imminent amid the upheaval at Old Trafford: Michael Carrick was sacked on Thursday, while Mauricio Pochettino is expected to take over as head coach. United will hope Pochettino’s arrival can persuade Fernandes to stay. The midfielder came close to joining Pochettino’s Tottenham in 2019, before moving from Sporting to United six months later. He has scored six goals in 13 appearances for United this season. BBC chief football news reporter Simon Stone says Fernandes wants to compete for the biggest prizes and will want to see what impact Pochettino has at United. The club, meanwhile, must weigh the cost and length of a new deal against Fernandes’ recent drop in form after an outstanding previous season, when he broke the Premier League assists record and won major player-of-the-year awards. Fernandes is 32, and a new contract could commit United to a substantial outlay over several years. Both sides may therefore have reasons to take their time, despite the club’s wish to keep its captain. The other family members who share the birthday are Wilber’s daughter, Addie Harlow, born on September 14, 1949; his grandson, Donald Harlow, born on September 14, 1972; and his great-granddaughter, Emma Bell, born on September 14, 1997. Arthur’s grandfather, Donald, also expressed his excitement, saying: “God works in beautiful ways.” The family’s birthday tradition began in 1907 when Wilber Harlow was born. nigeria.title: U-23 AFCONQ: Nigeria suffer 2-0 defeat to DR Congo in first leg
nigeria.description: Nigeria’s hopes of qualifying for the 2027 Under-23 Africa Cup of Nations suffered a setback on Friday after the Olympic Eagles lost 2-0 to DR Congo in the first leg of their second-round qualifying tie. The Nigerian side, led by Ikorodu City head coach Bright Osehai Ozebagbe and former Nigeria U-20 assistant coach Deniran Ortega, struggled to convert their early opportunities as the hosts secured a comfortable advantage ahead of the return fixture. The coaching duo took charge in the absence of Super Eagles manager Eric Chelle, who was occupied with Nigeria’s senior national team preparations for their crucial Africa Cup of Nations qualifier against Tanzania. Nigeria started brightly and nearly took the lead in the fourth minute when Victor Samuel’s effort missed the target. The midfielder had another opportunity five minutes later after finding himself one-on-one with the DR Congo goalkeeper but failed to convert. The missed chances proved costly as DR Congo took the lead in the 20th minute in controversial circumstances. Nigeria goalkeeper Samuel James appeared to have been fouled by a Congolese player while attempting to collect an aerial ball during the build-up to the opening goal. However, the referee allowed the goal to stand. The Olympic Eagles suffered another setback in the 30th minute when Brighton youngster Zadok Yohanna was forced off with an injury. DR Congo doubled their advantage five minutes before the break through Felozefe Mabete, who produced an impressive free-kick to put the hosts firmly in control. Despite their attempts to find a way back into the contest after the restart, Nigeria could not break down the Congolese defence, with the hosts protecting their two-goal advantage until the final whistle. The result leaves the Olympic Eagles with a difficult task in the second leg, as they must overturn the deficit to keep their qualification hopes alive. Nigeria will host DR Congo in the return fixture at the Remo Stars Stadium on Tuesday, where they will seek to secure an aggregate victory and advance to the final qualifying round. The Under-23 Africa Cup of Nations also serves as the qualification pathway for the men’s football tournament at the 2028 Summer Olympics in Los Angeles. nigeria.title: Boko Haram: Zulum announces ₦50k for each soldier deployed to Borno communities
nigeria.description: By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri Borno State Governor, Professor Babagana Umara Zulum, has announced ₦50,000 support to each soldier preparing for deployment to the two communities of Maiwa and Koshebe villages. Our Correspondent report that Koshebe in November 28, 2020 came under massacre when some armed Boko Haram militants launched a devastating attack on peasant and laborer rice farmers working in the fields (near Zabarmari and Maiduguri), where over 100 farm laborers—many of whom traveled from Sokoto State in northwest Nigeria for seasonal harvest work—were rounded up, tied, and their throats slit. Likewise, in November, 2023, suspected Boko Haram insurgents again targeted rice farmers harvesting crops in the Karkut and Koshebe general areas of Mafa Local Government Area, killing at least 13 farmers and leaving others missing. But Zulum assured that he will provide the needed support to strengthen security along the Maiduguri–Mafa–Dikwa–Ngala highway, ensure safe travel, and revive trade in communities recovering from years of insurgency. The Governor gave the assurance on Friday during a visit to the headquarters of the 24 Task Force Brigade in Dikwa Local Government Area where he met with the Brigade Commander, Brigadier General Aminu Gumel. “My visit is primarily aimed at exploring measures to strengthen security along the strategic economic corridor, which connects Maiduguri to several communities in eastern Borno and serves as a vital route for trade, transportation and cross-border commercial activities,” Zulum said. The highway links communities along the corridor to markets and facilitates the movement of agricultural produce, essential commodities and other goods. Zulum said improving security along the route would help residents travel safely, trade and rebuild their livelihoods. Addressing troops preparing for deployment to Maiwa and Koshebe villages, the governor pledged “to provide operational logistics and sustain welfare support. He announced ₦50,000 support to each soldier preparing for deployment to the two communities”. Governor Zulum’s administration has consistently supported military operations with logistics and welfare assistance as part of efforts to improve security and help displaced residents return to their communities. The Governor was accompanied on the visit by the member representing Monguno/Nganzai/Marte Federal Constituency in the House of Representatives, Engr Bukar Talba; member representing Dikwa Constituency in the State House of Assembly, Mohammed Zakariya; Commissioner for Information and Internal Security, Professor Usman Tar; Commissioner for Local Government and Emirate Affairs, Sugun Mai Mele; and other senior government officials. nigeria.title: Emefiele: Court admits Supreme Court judgment in alleged $4.5bn fraud trial
nigeria.description: An Ikeja Special Offences Court on Friday admitted a certified copy of a Supreme Court judgment linking former CBN Governor, Godwin Emefiele, to forfeited properties. Justice Rahman Oshodi admitted the judgment as Exhibit L after overruling objections by Emefiele’s defence counsel. Emefiele is facing a 19-count charge bordering on alleged gratification, corrupt demands and abuse of office involving $4.5 billion and N2.8 billion. His co-defendant, Henry Omoile, is facing a three-count charge of alleged unlawful acceptance of gifts. Oshodi ruled that the certified true copy of the Supreme Court judgment was admissible as a public document. He said the fact that only the lead judgment was tendered did not render it incomplete or inadmissible. The judge also addressed concerns about the prosecution’s reliance on a civil judgment in the ongoing criminal trial. He, however, restricted its use to establishing what the Supreme Court had decided in the previous proceedings. He stressed that the judgment could not constitute evidence for or against any party in the ongoing trial. “It has been well settled that court judgments are only used when tendered in a trial to determine and confirm what was actually decided in the case. “They are not used as evidence given in them for or against any of the parties therein,” Oshodi said. The Director of Public Prosecutions of the Federation, Mr Rotimi Oyedepo (SAN), had tendered the document through EFCC investigator, Mr Alvan Gurumnaan. However, Emefiele’s lead counsel, Mr Ojo Olalekan (SAN), opposed its admissibility, arguing that only four justices signed the judgment. He maintained that Supreme Court decisions were ordinarily delivered by panels of five or seven justices. Ojo also argued that the judgment arose from non-conviction forfeiture proceedings and was irrelevant to the prosecution’s case. Counsel to Omoile, Mr Adeyinka Kotoye (SAN), aligned himself with the objections and urged the court to reject the document. Kotoye argued that admitting the judgment could undermine the principle of estoppel and the defendants’ presumption of innocence. He also questioned the prosecution’s decision to introduce the document after proceedings had begun. Responding, Oyedepo argued that the document was a duly certified Supreme Court decision admissible under Sections 102 and 104 of the Evidence Act. Following the ruling, Gurumnaan faced cross-examination by Emefiele’s counsel over his role in the investigation. The witness said he personally obtained statements, analysed bank statements and coordinated other members of the investigation team. He confirmed interviewing Zenith Bank Managing Director, Dr Ebenezer Onyeagwu, but could not immediately recall whether a statement was obtained. Gurumnaan said the investigation involved hundreds of interviews with CBN officials, commercial bank employees and personnel of other government agencies. nigeria.title: Why I lied about having cancer – Blessing CEO
nigeria.description: By Wasiu Rokibat Nigerian social media personality Blessing Okoro, popularly known as Blessing CEO, has sparked fresh reactions after admitting that she falsely claimed to have breast cancer which in turn led to financial assistance from members of the public. The relationship influencer made the revelation during an interview with social media activist Martins Vincent Otse, better known as VeryDarkMan. Speaking during the interview, Blessing explained that although medical examinations discovered a lump in her breast, the result showed that it was not cancerous. However, she admitted that she deliberately presented the condition as cancer to attract sympathy from fans. In her words, “I do not have cancer. I had gone for a check-up and they found a lump in my breast, but it was not cancerous. I took advantage of that and told the public that the lump was cancerous. I played an emotional game.” According to her, she initially suggested that she might sell some of her personal belongings, including her car and house, before members of the public encouraged her to share her bank details for financial assistance. Blessing also disclosed that donations began coming in from different individuals but stopped after VeryDarkMan publicly questioned her cancer claims and demanded evidence of her diagnosis. “People had empathy, I did not come out to beg for funds. I played an emotional game. I wanted funds but I didn’t come out directly to ask for funds. I started with pretending I wanted to sell my personal belongings, my house, my car; It was fans who reached out to me in my DM, asking me to put out my account number; that’s when I put out my account number.” “The donation was rolling in, until VeryDarkMan came and say you people cannot be donating money for Blessing when there is no evidence. Immediately, VeryDarkMan made that video, the donation stopped. I am not proud of what I did.” The confession has renewed public attention to the controversy, which began in March 2026 when the influencer announced that she had breast cancer and appealed for financial support. She had previously acknowledged receiving about N13 million in donations but maintained that there had been confusion surrounding her medical condition. nigeria.title: FG Signs Port Harcourt Airport Concession Agreement, Assures Workers’ Protection
nigeria.description: The Federal Government has signed a concession agreement for the Jeremiah Obafemi Awolowo International Airport, Port Harcourt, with PH Airport Limited, following assurances from the concessionaire that the arrangement would not lead to job losses. The agreement was signed at the office of the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, in Abuja, on Thursday. The Federal Government delegation was led by Keyamo, while PH Airport Limited was represented by its Group Managing Director, Eyo Asuquo. The signing followed a meeting between the minister and aviation union leaders to discuss the implications of the concession for airport workers. Speaking on behalf of the unions, Comrade Ben Nnabue said organised labour had approved the agreement after receiving assurances that no aviation worker would lose their job as a result of the arrangement. He said job security remained a major concern for the unions and that they were satisfied with the commitments made before endorsing the agreement. Also speaking, Asuquo highlighted Port Harcourt’s strategic importance in the Gulf of Guinea, describing the airport as a potential gateway for regional commerce, investment and connectivity. He said PH Airport Limited intended to improve the airport’s infrastructure and operational standards, adding that the concession would create more employment opportunities rather than result in job losses. According to him, the company’s vision extends beyond managing the facility to expanding airport-related activities, attracting investment and unlocking its economic potential. The Director-General of the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority, Chris Najomo; Managing Director of the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria, Olubunmi Kuku; ministry directors and aviation union leaders attended the event. The $17 billion figure was down 21% from September and 48% from October 2025, when crypto notional volume reached $32.5 billion. It covers both the flagship Robinhood app and Bitstamp, the crypto exchange the company bought in 2025. Volume in the Robinhood app fell to $6.8 billion, down 24% from September and 51% from a year earlier. Bitstamp handled $10.2 billion, down 18% month over month and 45% year over year. Average daily crypto volume across both platforms came to $548 million, compared with $713 million in September and about $1.05 billion a year ago. Daily average crypto trades slipped to about 700,000 from 900,000 in September and 1.1 million in October 2025. Event contracts take off as crypto cools The contrast with Robinhood’s prediction markets business is stark. Customers traded 5.9 billion event contracts in October, up 5% from September and 136% from the 2.5 billion traded a year earlier. Average daily volume reached 190 million contracts. Robinhood counts crypto and prediction markets on the same 31-day calendar, since both trade every day, so the comparison is apples to apples. Event contracts let users bet on outcomes such as elections, sports and economic data, and October’s tally covered the final weeks before the Nov. 3 midterm elections. That growth has drawn scrutiny in Washington. Sen. Elizabeth Warren, who is set to chair the Senate Banking Committee in January, plans to crack down on prediction markets and election betting platforms. Total platform assets slipped 3% from September to $383 billion but were up 12% from a year earlier. Robinhood did not say why crypto activity fell. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine President Trump Taps Two Democrats in Bipartisan Slate of SEC and CFTC Nominees as Both Agencies Run Short-Handed President Donald Trump sent the Senate four nominees for the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission on Thursday, his first picks for either agency in about a year and the first Democrats he has put forward for them. Former CFTC Commissioner Kristin Johnson, a Democrat, and Republican Steven Levine were nominated to the SEC. Republican Nathan Anonick and Democrat Matthew Rowland were nominated to the CFTC, Bloomberg Law reported. Each nominee needs Senate confirmation. The Senate Banking Committee will handle the SEC picks, while the Senate Agriculture Committee will take up the CFTC pair before any vote by the full chamber. Who the nominees are Levine was tapped for the SEC seat left by Hester Peirce, whose term expired, for a term running through June 5, 2030. He most recently served as general counsel and a senior adviser at the White House Council of Economic Advisers and previously worked at the SEC as counsel and deputy chief of staff to Commissioner Mark Uyeda. Peirce led the SEC’s Crypto Task Force and was one of the agency’s most vocal supporters of clearer crypto rules. Johnson would take the seat formerly held by Democrat Caroline Crenshaw, for a term ending June 5, 2029. She served as a CFTC commissioner until 2025 and is a former law school professor. During her time at the CFTC, she spoke often about digital assets, including custody and decentralized finance. Both CFTC nominees come from the Senate Agriculture Committee, which oversees the derivatives regulator. Anonick is legislative counsel to Chairman John Boozman and was a lead negotiator on the committee’s portion of the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act. He was nominated to the seat once held by former Chairman Rostin Behnam, for a term ending June 19, 2031. Rowland is a CFTC attorney detailed to the committee who also worked on the Clarity Act and the committee’s 2024 crypto bill. He previously served on Johnson’s staff at the CFTC, according to his LinkedIn profile. He would fill the remainder of former Commissioner Summer Mersinger’s term, which expires April 13, 2028. Both agencies can seat up to five commissioners, with no more than three from one party. The SEC currently has two, Chairman Paul Atkins and Commissioner Mark Uyeda. Chairman Mike Selig is the CFTC’s only sitting commissioner. The campaign highlights how Hollandia Yoghurt can be enjoyed beyond a standalone beverage, featuring in breakfast options, snacks, smoothies and simple recipes. This consumer-focused approach is underpinned by Hollandia’s commitment to quality, with products carrying the masterbrand made with careful consideration and best-in-class quality processes. Speaking on the campaign, Olugbenga Akindele , Category Head, Dairy, said the initiative combines the brand’s focus on quality with an invitation for consumers to explore different ways to enjoy Hollandia Yoghurt. “At Hollandia, quality remains central to our commitment to consumers. Our products are made with careful consideration and best-in-class quality processes, reflecting our commitment to delivering products consumers can enjoy with confidence. Through our ‘Yoghurt It How You Want It’ campaign, we want consumers to discover more ways to enjoy Hollandia Yoghurt, whether as part of breakfast, a quick snack or their favourite food combinations, ” he said. Hollandia Yoghurt can be paired with popular snacks such as meat pies, sausage rolls and puff-puff, or combined with fruits and granola to create breakfast bowls and parfaits. It can also be blended with fruits to prepare smoothies or incorporated into selected recipes. The range offers consumers different flavour options to suit their preferences. Hollandia Strawberry brings a fruity taste to breakfast bowls and smoothies, while Hollandia Vanilla offers a creamy flavour for combinations such as pancakes, granola and parfaits. Hollandia Plain Sweetened provides another option for pairing with fruits, nuts and other toppings. Available in 315ml and 1L packs, Hollandia Yoghurt caters to different consumption occasions, from individual refreshment to household use and food preparation. Through the “Yoghurt It How You Want It ” campaign, Hollandia is encouraging consumers to explore different ways to incorporate Hollandia Yoghurt into their routines, with product quality remaining central to the brand’s commitment to Nigerian households. entertainment.title: Nigerian-Born Shirley Emehelu Makes History as New Jersey’s First Immigrant Lieutenant Governor
entertainment.description: Shirley U. Emehelu, New Jersey’s fifth Lieutenant Governor and Secretary of State. Photo Credit: Official Site of New Jersey A Nigerian-born legal leader has made history in New Jersey. New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill has officially appointed Nigerian-American Shirley U . Emehelu as the state’s fifth Lieutenant Governor and Secretary of State . Sworn in at the New Jersey Statehouse in Trenton on 9 November 2026, Emehelu has made double history in the process—becoming New Jersey’s first immigrant Lieutenant Governor and forming part of the state’s first all-women Governor–Lieutenant Governor team. Born in Nigeria before moving to the United States at the age of three, Emehelu brings an extraordinary record of public service and legal excellence to New Jersey’s second-highest executive office. Before this historic appointment, she served as Acting State Comptroller , leading key efforts to combat fraud, waste, and abuse while protecting taxpayer funds and strengthening government accountability, and also stepped in as Acting Secretary of State to oversee New Jersey’s elections. Her public sector résumé also includes a two-year tenure as Executive Assistant Attorney General of New Jersey, where she served as the third-ranking official in the New Jersey Attorney General’s Office. In that role, she directly counselled the Attorney General, coordinated oversight for more than 500 attorneys within the Division of Law—New Jersey’s largest legal office—and directed civil defence and enforcement matters across civil rights, environmental protection, labour and consumer protections, data privacy, and firearms safety. New Jersey Lieutenant Governor Shirley U. Emehelu, part of the state’s first all-women Governor–Lieutenant Governor team. Photo Credit: Shirley U. Emehelu/LinkedIn Earlier in her career, Emehelu spent nine years at the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of New Jersey, serving as Chief of Asset Recovery and Anti-Money Laundering, where she prosecuted complex financial fraud cases and oversaw statewide asset forfeiture and victim restitution programmes. She also practised in the private sector as a member of the White-Collar Criminal Defense and Government Investigations Group at CSG Law, co-leading the firm’s Banking and Finance Group, after clerking for the Honourable James R.Spencer in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia. An alumna of Yale University (where she earned her B.A.) and Yale Law School (where she earned her J.D.), Emehelu is a proud resident of Montclair, New Jersey, where she and her husband, Ike , raised their two children, Nnamdi and Amara . entertainment.title: FWIFT 2026 Convention Communique: Industry Leaders Charge Women in Media to Embrace Cross-Border Growth
entertainment.description: The Forum for Women in Film and Television Nigeria (FWIFT) successfully concluded its 2026 annual convention on Thursday, October 29, at the historic Glover Memorial Hall in Lagos, Nigeria. Convening under the theme “One Industry, Many Voices: Building Together,” the afternoon brought together over 200 practitioners from several sectors including; film, television, radio, advertising, and digital media to connect, share insights, and build mutual agency. Supported by the African Women’s Development Fund (AWDF) , the convention featured a keynote address by cultural curator Sandra Mbanefo Obiago , interactive panel sessions, break-out workshops, speed networking, and a flagship fireside chat titled “The Cross Over: A Career Beyond Borders.” The event drew leading voices from across the creative economy, including media executive Kadaria Ahmed , filmmaker Biodun Stephens, media personality Gbemi Olateru-Olagbegi, executive director Rosemary Egabor-Afolahan, and director Esosa Osagiede. Key takeaways and actionable resolutions from the convention sessions emphasized resilience, strategic partnerships, and structural evolution: Embrace Bold Collaboration and Risk-Taking: Speakers urged media professionals to shed apprehension around institutional partnerships. As highlighted during the panel discussions: “Do not allow fear of failing stop you from asking for help, do your due diligence on the people you want to partner with then go for it. If it does not work, do not stop, get up and go again.” Adaptability as a Survival Imperative: In an era of rapid technological and digital shifts across broadcast and film, participants were reminded of the absolute necessity of evolution: “If you don’t change with the times, you will grow stale.” Deconstructing Industry Myths: Addressing professional dynamics, panelists challenged antiquated narratives regarding female competition, affirming that systemic progress relies on solidarity: “Women work well with women, it is a myth that they do not.” FWIFT’s leadership noted that the conversations at Glover Memorial Hall mark a critical step toward cementing cross-sector alliances. The forum remains committed to translating these insights into actionable frameworks, mentorship programs, and policy advocacy for women shaping the future of African media. For more information on upcoming FWIFT initiatives, programs, and future events, visit the official website or follow @fwiftnigeria on social media. About FWIFT Nigeria The Forum For Women in Film and Television Nigeria (FWIFT) is a professional organization dedicated to empowering Nigerian women in screen-based, audio, and digital media through advocacy, skill acquisition, mentorship, and strategic networking. entertainment.title: Ayobami Esther Akinnagbe: Organisational Mistakes Start-up Founders Should Avoid
entertainment.description: Two women engaged in a professional meeting, discussing business in a modern office setting. Image by RDNE Stock project for Pexels . There is a lot that goes into establishing a successful business. It requires developing the business idea, securing clients, building a customer base and eventually bringing people on board. Starting a business and watching it grow can be an exciting experience. However, one thing many start-up founders overlook is the importance of having the right organisational structure in place. It is one thing to have a great business idea and attract talented employees, but it is another thing to create an environment where everyone understands their responsibilities, knows who they report to and can work effectively towards achieving the company’s objectives. I once worked with a client who needed a new set of employees for a business establishment that was reopening after a period of restructuring. As part of the recruitment process, the first thing I ensured was that a manager was hired before proceeding to fill the remaining vacancies. The idea was simple. The manager would oversee the day-to-day running of the establishment, ensure that company policies were implemented and periodically train employees based on the requirements of their respective roles. During the recruitment process, I clearly communicated each employee’s responsibilities and the person they would be reporting to. These details were also stated in their respective offer letters, so everyone understood their roles and the management structure they were expected to work within. However, there was a challenge. Before the manager was hired, an accountant who was personally known to both co-founders had also been in charge of the previous employees. Following the restructuring, the founders had communicated their desire for a new operational arrangement, and this was clearly reflected in the recruitment brief. Although the new employees understood that they were expected to report to the newly hired manager, the existing employees still had their loyalty to the accountant, who had previously been in charge. The challenge was that the new management structure had not been properly implemented within the organisation. entertainment.title: Uwaezu Kanu: Why Motherhood Feels Different for Women in Their 40s Today
entertainment.description: “Oh my God, Uwaezu! You need to hear the latest gist!” My younger sister buzzed with excitement. Though we had been living in different countries for a couple of years, we still made time to talk every single week. Unfortunately, when she called, I couldn’t talk on the phone as I had been ambushed by my kids, who were brandishing their homework and threatening to cry if I didn’t help them. As a mom herself, she immediately understood why I couldn’t continue with the conversation. I quickly made my excuses, and we laughed and hung up, promising to catch up at a more convenient time. However, that exchange got me thinking about how most millennial women have a radically different marriage and motherhood timeline from our mothers. You see, when my mother was in her early 40s, my siblings and I were in university, so she had a lot of free time during the week to spend relaxing, hanging out with her friends, and attending social events. Basically living her best life. I, on the other hand, at 40-plus, spend my days cooking pot after pot of hot meals that immediately get devoured by my ever-hungry kids, teaching my nursery school-aged kids how to count and spell, and trying but often failing to enforce a strict bedtime with yelling and threats. I constantly feel myself going underwater and have to fight for my life every single day. There are other ways motherhood has been such a hugely different experience for me than it was for my mother. Like many women of her generation, she got married right after secondary school as university education was not seen as vital. This meant that she was a teenage mother and so had more energy to spare on her kids. She also benefited from having a lot of support from domestic staff and relatives. I do not have any village supporting me with child-rearing. I have hired domestic staff in the past, but it was always one thing or another, and they ended up leaving me stranded. I also do not have youth on my side, and I have the back pain and other aches to prove it. But this experience is not unique to me. Statistics show that most women globally will have their first child at 30 or 31, and we are seeing a lot more women becoming first-time moms at 35 and above. This is considered advanced maternal age. The fact is that as women increasingly prioritise university education and career stability before marriage, maternal age will continue to rise. This is not a trend that can be reversed. entertainment.title: Toni Tones and Jim Iyke Are Bringing Drama to KAVA This November — See the Official Poster
entertainment.description: The Nigerian thriller series, directed by Wande Thomas and produced by Isoken Ogiemwonyi, is set to join KAVA’s growing slate of premium African content. Nigerian streaming platform KAVA is set to bring the psychological thriller series Spiraling , starring Toni Tones ( King of Boys ) and Jim Iyke , to audiences across its streaming service. Set against the high-stakes worlds of technology, power and politics in contemporary Nigeria, Spiraling follows Sade ( Toni Tones ), a brilliant tech entrepreneur whose carefully constructed life begins to unravel after an impulsive affair triggers a dangerous chain of events. Spiraling explores the darker side of ambition and the lengths people will go to protect their carefully constructed lives. Alongside Tones and Iyke, the ensemble cast includes Folu Storms , Seun Ajayi , Fae Olumide , Fiyinfoluwa Asenuga and Mathilda Akatugba . Created and directed by Wande Thomas ( Under the Influence , The Smart Money Woman ), the series is co-written by Thomas and Amaka Anioji and produced by Isoken Ogiemwonyi ( The Smart Money Woman , Ci ) . Director and creator Wande Thomas added: I wanted to explore how quickly an ordinary decision can spiral into something completely beyond your control. At its heart, this is a story about the secrets we keep, the lies we tell ourselves and how far we’ll go when everything is at stake. I’m excited for audiences to finally experience it. F Taofeeq/Spiraling Producer Isoken Ogiemwonyi said: With Spiraling , we wanted to take a simple story and tell it really well. We spent a lot of time developing the characters and exploring the darker side of very human emotions, ambition, desire and jealousy. At its heart, it’s a character-driven story about flawed people making questionable decisions, and we’re excited to partner with KAVA to bring it to audiences across Africa and the diaspora. Ladun Awobokun , Head of Acquisitions at KAVA commented : Spiraling is exactly the kind of bold, sophisticated African storytelling we want to champion at KAVA. With its compelling performances and distinctly Nigerian setting, the series delivers a gripping thriller that we believe will resonate with audiences at home and around the world. We’re delighted to bring it to our viewers. Spiraling will be available to stream on KAVA on the 26th of November. Follow @spiralingseries for updates. entertainment.title: “Lagos Gave Me My Greatest Successes and Deepest Heartbreak”: DJ Cuppy Opens Up in Ifeoluwa Documentary
entertainment.description: Nigerian DJ and philanthropist Florence Otedola, popularly known as Cuppy, pictured wearing gold headphones and a camel-brown blazer. On her birthday, Florence Ifeoluwa Otedola is giving viewers a more personal glimpse into her life, exploring home, family, identity and purpose. For years, Nigerians have known Florence “Cuppy” Otedola as the internationally recognised DJ and philanthropist, often recognised by her signature pink hair and vibrant public personality. This birthday, however, her new documentary offers a closer look at the woman behind that familiar public image. Released on 11 November 2026, her new 12-minute documentary, Ifeoluwa , follows Cuppy back to Lagos, the city that shaped her and remains close to her heart. It is also a place connected to some of her greatest successes and deepest heartbreak. The title Ifeoluwa means “The Love of God”. Rather than marking the occasion with another glamorous birthday celebration, Cuppy has chosen to share a more reflective portrait of her life. The film explores womanhood, ambition, identity, belonging and the ongoing process of becoming. There are tender moments, too. Viewers see Cuppy not just as a public figure, but as a daughter, sister and granddaughter. Her time with her grandmother offers an especially intimate glimpse into the affection and family ties at the heart of her story. The documentary also captures an evolution audiences may already have noticed. Her signature pink hair has given way to a new look, while faith, education and service have become increasingly central to how Cuppy speaks about her future. This is not a rejection of music, but a fuller picture of the person behind it. Her philanthropic work remains an important part of that picture. Through the Cuppy Foundation, she has helped raise more than $17 million to support displaced children in Nigeria, in partnership with Save the Children. She has also established education funds at the University of Oxford, New York University and King’s College London to help students overcome financial barriers, particularly those from Africa. Alongside this work, Cuppy remains active as an international DJ, with performances at Glastonbury, Wireless Festival and Cannes Lions, as well as events during United Nations General Assembly week. At its heart, Ifeoluwa is a personal homecoming that brings together family, faith, Lagos and the experiences shaping Cuppy’s next chapter. It offers viewers a chance to see beyond the familiar celebrity image and learn more about the person behind it. sports.description: Boston Red Sox outfielder Jarren Duran The Boston Red Sox have reportedly agreed to a four-year, $58 million deal with Jake Bauers. According to MassLive's Chris Cotillo , the Red Sox plan to use Bauers "primarily as their designated hitter while also cycling him in at first base in an effort to get Willson Contreras off his feet." If that's the case, Jarren Duran and Masataka Yoshida may need to pack their bags. Bauers plays first base and can fill in as a left fielder or right fielder. He'll be in the lineup every day, and if he's primarily taking the designated hitter spot, Duran and Yoshida will be bench bats or, at best, extra outfielders. The problem is, both will be very expensive bench players. Duran could end up getting $11.1 million in arbitration, per MLB Trade Rumors' estimate , and Yoshida is due $18.6 million next season. Those are some large figures for players who won't play regularly. The Red Sox have Roman Anthony, Ceddanne Rafaela and Wilyer Abreu in the outfield. Bauers can fill in if needed, and if the Red Sox don't want him there, they may much rather give Kristian Campbell a spot as the team's fourth outfielder. Campbell is already signed to an extension and started playing well in Triple-A toward the end of the season. Regardless, Duran and Yoshida simply don't have a path to regular at-bats with Bauers now on the team. Not only that, but neither one is really irreplaceable. sports.title: Tennessee on upset alert at Texas A&M, college football model warns
sports.description: On paper, you wouldn’t think that Tennessee was in any real danger against Texas A&M. Not when considering the general direction these teams have taken this season. But one of the most cited college football prediction models is taking a different view. Model projects a very close game Oct 17, 2026; Knoxville, Tennessee, USA; Tennessee Volunteers defensive back Dejuan Lane (10) celebrates after recovering a fumble against the Alabama Crimson Tide during the first half at Neyland Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Randy Sartin-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Looking over the matchup, ESPN’s College Football Power Index model still likes the Volunteers over the Aggies. But by a very narrow margin. After simulating the game 20,000 times, the model favors Tennessee to be just three points better than Texas A&M on the same field. That’s a much closer gap than most Vols fans would expect against an Aggie squad that has one win in SEC play. Normally, Tennessee is 13 points better than its opponents on average, ranking 17th in FBS in margin of victory. More: Predicting SEC football scores in Week 11’s biggest games Why such a close game? Tennessee has been extremely effective getting after opposing quarterbacks, but there’s one potential downside: the Volunteers have struggled at times to contain quarterbacks who can escape the pocket and extend plays. That’s where Marcel Reed becomes particularly dangerous. Tennessee’s defensive staff has acknowledged the challenge of defending mobile quarterbacks, emphasizing the importance of maintaining disciplined pass-rush lanes against Reed when he takes off. If Tennessee’s defensive ends get too aggressive pursuing the quarterback, Reed can step up, escape outside, and turn broken plays into significant gains. That creates two problems for the Volunteers: Scrambling yards: Reed can punish Tennessee when its pass rush loses lane discipline. Extended passing plays: When Reed escapes pressure, Tennessee’s secondary must cover receivers longer, increasing the possibility of explosive plays. More: SEC power rankings entering college football Week 11 The bottom line Texas A&M doesn’t necessarily need to beat Tennessee with traditional drop-back passing plays. The Aggies can use Reed’s mobility to neutralize some of Tennessee’s pass-rush advantage and force the Volunteers to defend the entire field. The potential breaking point: Tennessee’s inability to keep Marcel Reed contained inside the pocket. A narrow loss to the Washington Commanders hasn’t changed the fact that the New York Giants are in a strong position. However, John Harbaugh’s side could have looked to strengthen before the deadline, with ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler recently explaining what they were looking at and why it didn’t come to fruition. Vita Vea and Jeffery Simmons were among New York Giants targets says Jeremy Fowler When appearing on The Rich Eisen Show , Jeremy Fowler revealed that the New York Giants were looking at two positions before the deadline. They didn’t get a running back option through the door, though Cam Skattebo’s recent performances show that this position may not need strengthening at this time. Fowler did say that the other position in consideration for an “upgrade”, defensive tackle, was the bigger priority for the Giants. He added that Tampa’s Vita Vea and recent Chicago Bears addition Jeffery Simmons were both looked at as options. “At the end of the day, I don’t think they were really willing to give up what it would have taken to get any of those types of star players,” Fowler explained. May, who also works with Keegan Bradley, is based at Grove XXIII in Jupiter, Fla., where Koepka is a member. “Darren’s watched me from afar over the last few years and he’s got a really good understanding of the golf swing and how the body works,” Koepka told Golfweek . “When I was frustrated and trying to figure things out, his was the only name that popped into my head. It’s only been a short time, but it’s been very good.” More: Brooks Koepka calls his performance in PGA Tour return 'pathetic' The pair began working together after Koepka’s last competitive outing, which was the Alfred Dunhill Links on the DP World Tour in October. That week in St. Andrews saw his best finish of the year, a tie for 6th place. Koepka began seeing Faxon in August, shortly after failing to qualify for the FedEx Cup playoffs. Pete Cowen, who worked with Koepka on his full swing after the former world No. 1 split from Claude Harmon III in late 2024, remains his short game instructor. Koepka will play next week at the RSM Classic in Sea Island, Georgia. It will be his first start on the PGA Tour since the Wyndham Championship in August. He has struggled for form since returning to the PGA Tour in January after four seasons with LIV Golf. In 15 starts, he had just one top-10 finish, a tie for 9th at the Cognizant Classic in March. He had five other top-20 finishes, but for most of the year he’s been vocally unhappy with his putting. “Absolutely horrendous,” was how he described his performance on the greens at the PGA Championship in May. “Zero confidence. Can’t putt,” he said after missing the playoffs. He ranked 131st on Tour in Strokes Gained Putting for the season. Koepka switched from the blade-style putter he’d used throughout his career to a mallet putter at the WM Phoenix Open in February. He returned to using the blade after this first session with Faxon, shortly before he traveled to Europe for three tournaments. “We had an idea of the process we wanted to do to free me up. It wasn’t about the result those three weeks but freeing myself up,” he said. “And it has. It’s really been freeing to clear a lot of thoughts out of my head.” “Brooks and I have spent some time together and I’ll leave it at that,” Faxon said when contacted by Golfweek . Koepka is scheduled to play the Farmers Insurance Skins Game on Nov. 27 and will make his debut in the PNC Championship alongside his father, Bob, in Orlando from Dec. 17-20. technology.title: Mozilla leaves Solo website owners to go it alone as hosting shuts down
technology.description: Solo, Mozilla's LLM-powered website builder and hosting service, is shutting down. All sites and data will be deleted on November 30. Mozilla launched Solo in December 2023 as a "Mozilla Innovation Project," aimed at helping sole traders to build themselves a webpage for their services. S ome 54,000 people used its LLM to build pages, and relied on Mozilla to host them – complete with custom domain names. Well, not any more. Now the Soloist.ai homepage says: "We've made the difficult decision to close Solo. We have appreciated all of your support building and growing this product, and the feedback we've received from all of you. Solo will cease operations on Nov 30, 2026." Users now have just over two weeks left to find a new home for their pages, although Mozilla says it first notified them on October 1. According to the support FAQ , users can download a ZIP containing an HTML export, contact form and newsletter submissions, and a CSV linking to their images. The images themselves must be downloaded separately. Domains purchased through Solo Domains must also be moved to Name.com , with Mozilla handling the transfer after users create an account and supply its code. So much for having the fiddly bits taken care of. It also points at a couple of other bot-based site-generating services – in case all this feels like a bit too much. We suspect that for the sort of technophobes that this was aimed at, it very probably will. Mozilla told The Register : "Experimentation is an important part of Mozilla's mission to make the internet better and give people more choice and control online. Sometimes, that means making the decision to bring a product to an end. Solo will officially shut down on November 30, 2026. We initially notified customers on October 1, providing a 60-day transition period, and have been offering support to help them download their website data and migrate their domains purchased via Solo Domains to another hosting provider." It seems that some 54,000 users were not enough to keep it going, and we can see that this would cost money to keep running. An HTML export is a start, though the FAQ doesn't explain how much work it will take to get a complete, functioning site running elsewhere. Buried in the dark recesses of the web is this vulture's own nearly 30-year-old homepage, created using a mixture of Claris Home Page (which was excellent) and Microsoft FrontPage (ever so slightly less so). We saw what a mess machine-generated web content was back then, and thanks to LLMs, we suspect it is almost infinitely worse now. Mozilla might have made a few bucks by finding a commercial partner to take on its users, and perhaps through them offer a paid site-and-domain transfer service. As we noted last year, it seems not to have negotiated anything with KaiOSTech, which maintains and sells what used to be the formerly FOSS FirefoxOS for use on low-end smartphones.
